title: Implement declarative stage signatures, prompt budgets, and the provider port

checks.name: stage_signatures_declared
checks.evidence: stage_signatures() freezes exactly I0, E0, S1, B0 and B1. I0 is an internal FactExtractionDraft signature; the other four remain creative Draft stages.

checks.name: prompt_schema_separate_transport
checks.evidence: PromptCompiler transmits only contract identity and schema digest in prompt text. ClaudeDeepSeekStructuredAdapter sends the registered JSON Schema through StructuredTransportRequest.json_schema; tests prove canonical schema JSON is absent from system and user prompt fields.

checks.name: b1_prompt_under_12000_chars
checks.evidence: Stage.B1 declares a 12000-character hard prompt budget. The compiler measures complete system plus user text before provider I/O and the registered test proves a 12000-character oversized input fails closed.

checks.name: b1_schema_under_4500_chars
checks.evidence: Stage.B1 declares a 4500-character Schema budget. DraftSchemaRegistry canonicalizes and measures the separate ExecutionDesignDraft schema before provider I/O; its current canonical size is 2777 characters.

checks.name: native_windows_binary_first
checks.evidence: resolve_windows_claude_binary accepts only native claude.exe on Windows and rejects .cmd-only candidates. The native-only adapter rejects absent native JSON Schema capability before runner invocation even when a caller sets require_native_schema=false.

checks.name: one_scoped_contract_repair
checks.evidence: Repair now compiles the ViolationSet into a separate ContractPatch transport schema and returns a locally validated ContractPatch. RepairBudget permits exactly one successful scoped patch; transport failure consumes no budget and a second attempt fails before model I/O.

checks.name: i0_fact_extraction_signature
checks.evidence: I0 has a 6000-character prompt and 2500-character Schema cap, uses a non-Director fact-extraction core, disables creative fragments, and accepts only a closed FactExtractionDraft facts[] object with source span, semantic type, statement, and optional subject/dialogue/scene fields.

checks.name: source_span_repair_ceiling
checks.evidence: An I0 source_end violation is sent only as ViolationSet metadata. The repair request uses ContractPatch rather than FactExtractionDraft, returns only the whitelisted $.facts[0].source_end value, records attempt=2, and cannot be repeated after budget consumption.

informational_results.name: failure_first_v22_baseline
informational_results.result: Before the A4 implementation change, the expanded suite had 7 failures and 9 passes: I0 was absent and repair still requested a full Draft schema after receiving a patch-shaped input.

informational_results.name: a0_to_a4_and_v4_regression_local
informational_results.result: 105 passed in 6.93s; the v4 production entrypoint isolation suite remains green.

informational_results.name: scope_and_diff_hygiene_local
informational_results.result: No whitespace errors. Only the seven A4 implementation/test paths and this A4 Evidence file are declared; unrelated dirty files are preserved and excluded.

findings: The prior A4 surface defined only E0, S1, B0 and B1, so v2.2's mandatory internal I0 FactExtractionDraft signature and closed fact-only Schema were absent.

The previous repair path accepted a pre-built ContractPatch but invoked generate() with the original full Draft schema. It could therefore send patch-shaped input while soliciting a whole Draft and did not mechanically enforce a source-span repair ceiling.
Native schema capability could be bypassed by setting GenerationPolicy.require_native_schema=false even though this named adapter has no safe non-native fallback transport.
The strict local decoder did not enforce declared string minLength, allowing an empty I0 statement despite the fact-only contract requiring source-supported content.
review.root_cause: A4 was previously completed for the v2.1 four-stage creative flow. The v2.2 rebase introduced a typed ingest boundary, but the old implementation treated it as an optional prompt variation and treated repair as an input-patch helper rather than a separately schema-constrained model response.

considered_options.option: Fold I0 into an existing Director creative stage or restore a combined total prompt
considered_options.reason: It would erase the architecture's explicit source-anchored ingest boundary and violate the stage-scoped prompt design.

considered_options.option: Keep full Draft responses for repair and filter changed fields after the call
considered_options.reason: The model would still receive/return unbounded Draft authority, so neither the one-repair limit nor source-span repair ceiling would be provable at the transport boundary.

considered_options.option: Create a frozen I0 Signature with a separate FactExtractionDraft Schema and compile repairs against a separate ContractPatch Schema
considered_options.reason: It preserves one structured port, strict budget gates and locally auditable limited repair without creating a persistent I0 node or adding creative authority to ingest.

considered_options.option: Offer an implicit text/JSON fallback when native Schema capability is absent
considered_options.reason: This adapter is native-schema-only; a fallback would weaken the declared transport contract and must be designed as a separate future adapter if ever authorized.

remaining_risks: A4 validates only the bounded model contract and patch ceiling. A8's normalized-source ingest and local FactAssembler must verify non-empty ordered spans, source support, dialogue-specific fields and deterministic fact identity before persistent FactRegistry output.

A4 does not call a model, Shadow, media service or production switch. Later runtime work must reuse stage_signatures() rather than reconstructing signatures or treating TextCallEvidence as visual evidence.
I0's 6000/2500 stage limits are deliberately conservative and fail rather than truncate; A8 must split independent normalized-source windows when an input would exceed the frozen budget.
